data.why: The repo ships real measured single-spectrum CSVs (256-point absorbance, no header) plus a batch file and blank template that are exactly what the Predict tab's uploader expects; no synthetic data is needed.

goals: Screen a Haridra dry extract spectrum for starch adulteration and get a quantitative % w/w estimate with a confidence zone
Judge whether a prediction falls inside the validated calibration range or is extrapolating
Understand how SNV preprocessing removes scattering/packing variation versus raw absorbance
Pick the number of PLS latent variables by inspecting the RMSECV-vs-complexity curve rather than taking a default on faith
Assess curcuminoid assay linearity and know the working range imposed by its absolute error floor
Review model provenance, intended use and limitations before trusting a result

review.summary: The tree captures this tool's purpose well: starch screening with a confidence zone, judging trust through RPD, RMSECV and LV choice, SNV inspection, the curcuminoid working range, and the model card. Most cited screens match their nodes. Before filing it needs fixes: the batch_7 upload behaviour is wrong in both a task and a feature (it crashes rather than showing a hint, as the code and the replay confirm), one action cites the wrong screen, and the RED zone and wrong-length rejection paths were never reached.
